Nitecore NWL20

Reverse Engineering a Work Light

I wanted to understand how a work light’s housing, hinge, and internal components fit together.

Dates
April–May 2026
Course
MCEN 1025
My Role
Individual project
Deliverables
16 parts · 2 subassemblies · 5 drawings

Nitecore designed the original work light. I created the CAD model and drawings shown here.

On This PageProject OverviewMeasurement & ModelingModeling ChallengesEngineering DrawingsResults & Lessons Learned
01 / Overview

Project Overview

I chose the NWL20 because I could take it apart and see how features like the magnetic base, 180-degree hinge, and carabiner were built. My goal was to recreate the parts and their assembly in SOLIDWORKS.

02 / Process

Measurement & Modeling

I disassembled the light and measured the parts with calipers. I had to work around the circuit board and wires to reach some of the housing dimensions. I then put the modeled parts together in CAD to see how they fit.

03 / Challenges

Modeling Challenges

The housing changes shape along its length and has very little symmetry. When I got stuck on a detail, I broke the shape down into simpler geometry and tried building it one feature at a time.

During development, I used the rollback bar to step back to an earlier point in the model. I also used feature suppression to temporarily take a modeling step out of the build. Both let me compare different ways to make a shape before choosing the approach I wanted to keep.

For the button on the outside of the housing, I used a fill pattern to repeat a detail within the button’s outline. I used draft cuts to recreate the slight taper on the housing. That angle gives an injection-molded part clearance as it comes out of the mold.

Several parts mount to the housing, so small measurement errors caused parts to overlap in the assembly. Where parts collided, I went back to the measurements and adjusted the dimensions of the mounting features.

04 / Documentation

Engineering Drawings

I used detail views to enlarge small features so I could dimension them without crowding the main views. Section views showed the internal features and how the housing geometry changes through the part.

05 / Results

Results & Lessons Learned

I modeled the buttons as part of the housing and left out the rubber seals and their grooves. The button pattern and material appearances also differ from the physical light. Those were limits of the model I documented alongside the assembly.

Trying different ways to build a feature took longer than I expected, and the drawings took about as much time as the modeling. I learned to budget time for both and decide which small details were worth modeling.
